_about: The world lane: the powers that ruled over or pressed on Israel (empires), and the foreign rulers Scripture names or plainly means (rulers). Empire spans are the years each mattered to the land, not the whole life of the state. Dates are standard ancient-history dates; `approx` where those are themselves uncertain. `ref` is where Scripture names or describes them.

empires.name: Ur (Third Dynasty)
empires.summary: The Sumerian kingdom at its height around Ur of the Chaldees, which Abram's family left.

empires.name: Egypt (Middle Kingdom)
empires.summary: A strong, united Egypt: the Pharaohs of Abram's visit and of Joseph's rise.

empires.name: Hyksos rule in Egypt
empires.summary: Semitic rulers in the Nile delta; perhaps why a new king arose 'who did not know Joseph' after they were driven out.

empires.name: Egypt (New Kingdom)
empires.summary: The empire of the great Pharaohs: the oppression, the plagues and the Exodus.

empires.name: Assyria
empires.summary: The Neo-Assyrian empire: Nineveh, Jonah's preaching, the deportation of the ten tribes and the siege of Jerusalem.

empires.name: Babylon
empires.summary: Nebuchadnezzar's empire: the exile of Judah and the destruction of Jerusalem and the Temple.

empires.name: Persia
empires.summary: From Cyrus to Darius III: the return from exile, the second Temple, Esther and Nehemiah.

empires.name: Alexander's Greece
empires.summary: The goat from the west with one great horn: Alexander conquers the whole Persian empire in a decade.

empires.name: The Ptolemies (Egypt)
empires.summary: Daniel's 'kings of the south': Judea is ruled from Alexandria for a century, and the Septuagint is made there.

empires.name: The Seleucids (Syria)
empires.summary: Daniel's 'kings of the north': Judea passes to Antioch, and Antiochus IV tries to stamp out the Law.

empires.name: Hasmonean kingdom
empires.summary: Independent Judea under the Maccabees' family, priest-kings for eighty years until Rome arrives.

empires.name: Rome
empires.summary: Pompey takes Jerusalem in 63 BC; Herod, the census, Pilate, Paul's appeal to Caesar and the fall of Jerusalem follow.

rulers.name: Shishak (Shoshenq I)
rulers.title: Pharaoh of Egypt
rulers.summary: Sheltered Jeroboam, then plundered the Temple's treasures in Rehoboam's fifth year.

rulers.name: Tiglath-pileser III (Pul)
rulers.title: King of Assyria
rulers.summary: Took tribute from Menahem, carried Galilee into exile, and was paid by Ahaz to attack Damascus.

rulers.name: Shalmaneser V
rulers.title: King of Assyria
rulers.summary: Besieged Samaria for three years when Hoshea stopped paying tribute.

rulers.name: Sargon II
rulers.title: King of Assyria
rulers.summary: Completed the fall of Samaria and resettled the land with foreigners, who became the Samaritans.

rulers.name: Sennacherib
rulers.title: King of Assyria
rulers.summary: Took forty-six cities of Judah and shut Hezekiah up 'like a bird in a cage'; his army died in one night outside Jerusalem.

rulers.name: Esarhaddon
rulers.title: King of Assyria
rulers.summary: Sennacherib's son, who succeeded him after his brothers murdered him at prayer.

rulers.name: Ashurbanipal (Osnappar)
rulers.title: King of Assyria
rulers.summary: The last great Assyrian king; probably the one whose commanders took Manasseh to Babylon in chains.

rulers.name: Neco II
rulers.title: Pharaoh of Egypt
rulers.summary: Killed Josiah at Megiddo on his way to help Assyria, then made Jehoiakim king; beaten by Nebuchadnezzar at Carchemish.

rulers.name: Nebuchadnezzar II
rulers.title: King of Babylon
rulers.summary: Took Daniel, then Jehoiachin, then Jerusalem itself; humbled to eat grass like an ox until he praised the Most High.

rulers.name: Evil-merodach (Amel-Marduk)
rulers.title: King of Babylon
rulers.summary: Released Jehoiachin from prison and gave him a seat at the king's table.

rulers.name: Belshazzar
rulers.title: Co-regent of Babylon
rulers.summary: Feasted from the Temple's vessels on the night Babylon fell; the writing on the wall said his kingdom was finished.

rulers.name: Cyrus the Great
rulers.title: King of Persia
rulers.summary: Took Babylon in 539 and decreed that the Jews could go home and rebuild the Temple, as Isaiah had named him to do.

rulers.name: Darius I
rulers.title: King of Persia
rulers.summary: Found Cyrus's decree in the archives and ordered the Temple finished at royal expense.

rulers.name: Xerxes I (Ahasuerus)
rulers.title: King of Persia
rulers.summary: Esther's husband, ruler from India to Ethiopia, who let Haman's decree be answered.

rulers.name: Artaxerxes I
rulers.title: King of Persia
rulers.summary: Sent Ezra with the Law in 458 and his cupbearer Nehemiah to rebuild the walls in 445.

rulers.name: Alexander the Great
rulers.title: King of Macedon
rulers.summary: The 'mighty king' of Daniel 11:3, who conquered Persia and died at thirty-two with no heir; his kingdom was divided four ways.

rulers.name: Antiochus IV Epiphanes
rulers.title: Seleucid king
rulers.summary: Daniel's 'contemptible person': banned the Law, set up an altar to Zeus in the Temple, and provoked the Maccabean revolt.

rulers.name: Herod the Great
rulers.title: King of Judea
rulers.summary: Rome's client king: rebuilt the Temple on a grand scale, and killed the boys of Bethlehem.

rulers.name: Caesar Augustus
rulers.title: Emperor of Rome
rulers.summary: The first emperor, whose decree of a census brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem.

rulers.name: Herod Archelaus
rulers.title: Ethnarch of Judea
rulers.summary: So brutal that Joseph would not settle in Judea under him; Rome deposed him after ten years.

rulers.name: Herod Antipas
rulers.title: Tetrarch of Galilee
rulers.summary: Beheaded John the Baptist; Jesus called him 'that fox' and stood silent before him at his trial.

rulers.name: Tiberius
rulers.title: Emperor of Rome
rulers.summary: Emperor through Jesus's ministry and death: the Caesar on the coin.

rulers.name: Pontius Pilate
rulers.title: Prefect of Judea
rulers.summary: Found no guilt in Jesus, washed his hands, and handed him over to be crucified.

rulers.name: Herod Agrippa I
rulers.title: King of Judea
rulers.summary: Killed James the brother of John and imprisoned Peter; struck down at Caesarea when the crowd called him a god.

rulers.name: Claudius
rulers.title: Emperor of Rome
rulers.summary: Emperor of the great famine, who expelled the Jews from Rome; that is how Aquila and Priscilla came to Corinth.

rulers.name: Antonius Felix
rulers.title: Governor of Judea
rulers.summary: Kept Paul in custody at Caesarea for two years, hoping for a bribe.

rulers.name: Nero
rulers.title: Emperor of Rome
rulers.summary: The Caesar Paul appealed to; after the fire of Rome in 64 he blamed and killed the Christians.

rulers.name: Porcius Festus
rulers.title: Governor of Judea
rulers.summary: Heard Paul's case and sent him to Caesar, after Agrippa said he could have been set free.

rulers.name: Herod Agrippa II
rulers.title: King
rulers.summary: 'Almost you persuade me to be a Christian.'

rulers.name: Domitian
rulers.title: Emperor of Rome
rulers.summary: The emperor under whom John was exiled to Patmos, by the usual dating of Revelation.
